Spinal Cord Injury Classification According to ASIA

Spinal cord injury classification

  • ASIA classification of spinal cord injury is the gold standard nowadays to classify these injuries
  • To classify spinal cord injury according to American spinal injury association, neurological examination has to be done looking for sensory or motor deficits
  • Motor examination is done using muscle power of the key muscles only looking for any motor deficits
  • Sensory examination is done using superficial modality (pinprick) and deep modality (touch) only looking for any deficits

Key muscles

Table from slide 3
C5Elbow flexors
C6Wrist extensors
C7 Elbow extensors
C8 Finger flexors
T1 5th finger abductors
L2 Hip flexors
L3Knee extensors
L4 Ankle dorsiflexors
L5Big toe extensors
S1Ankle plantar flexors

Neurological examination

  • Muscle power is graded out of 5 according to the MRC grading
  • 0/5: no muscle movement
  • 1/5: visible muscle movement but with no movement at the joint
  • 2/5: movement at the joint but not against gravity
  • 3/5: movement against gravity, but not against added resistance
  • 4/5: movement against resistance, but less than normal
  • 5/5: normal power
  • Sensory is graded out of 2 according to
  • 0: absent sensation
  • 1: altered
  • 2: normal

Classify by following these steps

  • Determine the sensory levels for right and left sides (each side graded independently), intact dermatome must be responding to pinprick and light touch sensation
  • Determine the motor levels for right and left sides (each side graded independently), motor level defined by the lowest key muscle (on the body) with grade 3 power and the muscles above this muscle are grade 5 power
  • Determine the neurological level of injury: NLI refers to the lowest segment with intact sensation and motor function (grade 3 muscle power), NLI is the lower level of the sensory and motor levels assigned in step 1 and 2
  • Determine if the injury is complete or incomplete: if patient can’t voluntarily contract anal sphincter and sensory exam of S4, S5 is 0 and deep anal pressure is negative then injury is complete, otherwise injury is incomplete
  • Now you can determine the injury grade according to ASIA impairment scale

ASIA impairment scale (AIS)

Table from slide 8
Grade Description
A Complete: no sensory or motor at S4-5
BSensory incomplete: sensory is preserved below neurological level of injury including sensation at S4-5, but motor function is preserved only to three levels below the motor level on either side of the body
C Motor incomplete: motor is preserved at the S4-5 or the patient sensory is preserved at S4-5 with preservation of more than 3 motor levels below the level of injury (less than half key muscles below level of injury have muscle power equals to 3 or more)
D Motor incomplete: same as AIS C with more than half of the key muscles below level of injury have muscle power grade of 3 or more
ENormal
